plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Bare branches burst into clouds of white-to-blush blossoms before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like snow and cover paths and ponds in pale pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April, with peak bloom in Japan's main cities from late March into early April
plants.location: Japan, including Tokyo, where it is the classic tree of hanami (flower-viewing) parties
plants.funFact: Most Yoshino cherries are clones grafted from one original tree. Trees in the same area therefore tend to open at almost the same moment, which is why the bloom seems to sweep across a city in a few days.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: Silky, cup-shaped flowers glow like molten gold. They open in the sun and carpet hillsides and grasslands in fiery orange. Their feathery blue-green foliage sets off the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom is March to May, and flowers can appear earlier or later depending on rainfall
plants.location: California and the western United States, in grasslands, foothills and open meadows
plants.funFact: The petals fold shut on cloudy days and at night, then open again in sunshine. It is the official state flower of California.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Tall, bare, plum-colored stems rise without leaves and carry fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. The display is dramatic and often follows the first autumn rains.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, around March to April, depending on rainfall
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa, and Mediterranean-climate gardens in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The flowers are nicknamed 'naked lady' because they bloom on leafless stalks. The foliage grows only after flowering, a reversal of the usual order.
